subject: Dedicated capacity: Clusterly peak profile & token sample request
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom@clusterly.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Clusterly -- peak concurrency & typical prompt/response profile

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. To move toward a reserved capacity proposal we put together our rough traffic profile below and can share a token-level export if that helps with sizing. Quick summary: 

- Peak sustained RPS: ~500 requests/sec for a 90-minute daily window (regional peak, PST)
- Average prompt length: 70-90 tokens (median ~78)
- Average response length: 160-210 tokens (p95 ~340)
- Session behavior: ~35% of requests reuse a recent KV context across the same session; average session duration ~45s
- Retries/backoff: clients will retry once after 300ms if no response; ~3% retries observed in past weeks
- Availability target: p95 latency < 350ms for interactive flows; p99 < 800ms is ideal

We expect to sign a 12-month reserved commitment if the baseline capacity covers the 500 RPS window with a burst pool for 2x. We can share a sample week of request/response token logs (anonymized) and a brief heatmap of hourly traffic.

Can you confirm what additional telemetry you need (token counts by request, timestamps, session id) and whether a 48-72h performance run on your side is required before final commit?

Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, Clusterly
ops@clusterly.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom@clusterly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clusterly -- peak concurrency & typical prompt/response profile

Tom — thanks, that profile is very helpful. A few clarifying questions so our pre-sales sizing can be tighter: 

1) Token distribution: can you share percentiles (p50/p90/p95) for prompt and response token counts?  The p95 you gave for responses helps; p50 will let us optimize batching/kv cache tradeoffs.
2) Mix of traffic: what fraction is interactive (single-request, low latency) vs. async/batch (higher latency okay)?
3) Session affinity: when you say 35% reuse, is that measured on a per-session key (user id) or by repeated prompts in the same session id? Also, typical kv cache reuse TTL?
4) Peak concurrency: can you convert the 500 RPS into concurrent open sessions we should expect (approx)?
5) Fault tolerance: any regional failover requirements or desire for cross-region fallback?

I attached a short CSV template (redwood_sizing_template.csv) that captures the fields we use to run through our sizing model — if you can drop the token export into that layout it speeds things up. Once we ingest the sample we'll share a rough fleet footprint (GPU SKU mix, reserved vs. burst split, suggested cache sizing) and recommend a 48h pilot to validate queuing behavior.

Next steps: if you can drop the sample + the filled template into the Drive link I sent we can aim to deliver a draft sizing within 72 business hours.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com
From: Tom Ellis <tom@clusterly.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@clusterly.com
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clusterly -- peak concurrency & typical prompt/response profile

Hannah — attaching the anonymized token export as requested (clusterly_token_sample_week.csv) and a PNG heatmap of hourly RPS (traffic-heatmap-may2026.png). Answers inline below: 

1) Token percentiles (week sample): prompt p50=75, p90=120, p95=170. response p50=150, p90=300, p95=340.
2) Mix: ~82% interactive flows (low latency, single-turn), ~18% async (batch jobs, acceptable latency up to 10s).
3) Reuse: 35% measured by session id (we persist session ids for 10 minutes by default). KV cache TTL ~10 minutes; most reuse is within first 2 mins.
4) Concurrent open sessions during peak: rough telemetry shows ~1,100-1,350 concurrent WebSocket sessions during the 90-minute window; average concurrent active requests ~420 (locks to RPS/processing time).
5) Failover: we prefer single-region commit (US-West) with a cross-region read-only fallback if needed; no strict synchronous multi-region commit required.

We are comfortable committing to a 12-month reserved tier covering ~60% of sustained peak if the remainder can be handled by a burst pool (we'd like to avoid paying for 100% reserved).

Tom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom@clusterly.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clusterly -- peak concurrency & typical prompt/response profile

Thanks for the sample, Tom — helpful dataset. Preliminary sizing notes (high-level, ballpark):

- Workload characteristics: high fraction interactive, moderate response sizes with long p95 tail. KV reuse (35%) will materially reduce per-token cost for repeated context; we should account for warm KV cache on ~30% of requests.
- Rough committed footprint recommendation (sustained 60% of your peak + headroom): estimate ~18-28x high-memory GPUs depending on SKU (examples: A100-80GB or equivalent H100 mixes). Exact SKU and oversubscription depend on your latency SLO and whether we enable quantization.
- Burst pool: 1.5-2x the committed capacity for burst windows to keep p99s acceptable during the 90-minute peaks.
- Operational asks: enable token-level logging for the pilot (anonymized), allow us to run a 48h stress with representative traffic to validate queuing and batching behavior.

Questions for the proposal: what's your preferred monthly commit (vCPU equivalent) and any hard budget constraints? Also confirm if you want us to size for p99 latency targets or prioritize cost and accept higher p99s during peak.

I'll draft a quick sizing baseline and share later today — we can then schedule a 30-min alignment to go over numbers.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Clusterly -- peak concurrency & typical prompt/response profile

Tom — we reviewed the sample and Karthik put together a preliminary footprint. Proposed next steps: 

1) We will send a short baseline sizing doc (ballpark GPU counts / suggested SKU mix + burst split) by EOD Tuesday.
2) If that looks reasonable, we schedule a 30-minute technical alignment (we have open slots Wed 9:30-11:00 or Thu 13:00-15:00 PT).
3) With your go-ahead we'll run a 48-hour pilot (anonymized traffic) to validate latency and queueing; results will be used for final proposal and pricing.

I'll attach the baseline doc to the Drive link and post the calendar invite once you confirm the time. Thanks again — excited to get this moving.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
